Musical artist

**Sergio Franchi** ([US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English "American English"): [/ˈ f r ɑː ŋ k i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FRAHNG-kee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), Italian:[[ˈsɛrdʒo ˈfraŋki]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born **Sergio Franci Galli**; April 6, 1926 – May 1, 1990) was an Italian-American [tenor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenor "Tenor") and actor who enjoyed success in the United States and internationally after gaining notice in Britain in the early 1960s. In 1962, [RCA Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Victor "RCA Victor") signed him to a seven-year contract and in October of that year Franchi appeared on _[The Ed Sullivan Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ed\_Sullivan\_Show "The Ed Sullivan Show")_ and performed at [Carnegie Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Hall "Carnegie Hall"). [Sol Hurok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sol_Hurok "Sol Hurok") managed Franchi's initial American concert tour.

Franchi became a headliner in Las Vegas, and starred in concerts and cabarets on several continents. His earliest ambitions and studies had been directed toward an operatic career, but he instead found his niche in popular and [romantic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_music "Romantic music"). Franchi performed musical comedies on stage, appeared on numerous television variety shows, and starred in a major motion picture. He became an American citizen in 1972. After gaining success, Franchi was a benefactor and philanthropist, donating his time and talent to many causes. For his longtime support of Boys' and Girls' Towns of Italy, he was posthumously awarded the title of cavaliere in the Order of Merit (Stella al merito del lavoro) by the Italian Government.

## Early life in Italy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life in Italy")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Young_Sergio_Franchi_in_Italy.jpg/250px-Young_Sergio_Franchi_in_Italy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Young_Sergio_Franchi_in_Italy.jpg)

Young Sergio Franci Galli in Italy in 1936

Sergio Franci Galli was one of three children born to a [Neapolitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples") father and [Genoese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") mother.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Ed-1) Sergio, Mirella, and [Fausta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Valery "Dana Valery") (17 years younger than the elder siblings) were all born in the region of [Lombardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombardy "Lombardy"). This includes [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), [Cremona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cremona "Cremona"), and the smaller village of [Codogno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codogno "Codogno") – where he was born. Some geographical over-simplifications resulted in listing Franchi's birthplace as Cremona, and Fausta's birthplace as "near Milan".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Sun-2) Because the family also lived in Cremona, Franchi called both Codogno and Cremona his "hometown" at different periods in his life.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3) Franchi stated for the record several times in later life that his birthplace was Codogno in the province of [Lodi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodi,_Lombardy "Lodi, Lombardy").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Codogno-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Alassio-6) An uncle who owned a vineyard in [Alassio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alassio "Alassio"), on the [Italian Riviera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Riviera "Italian Riviera"), was instrumental in family life on various occasions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Sun-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Alassio-6)

As a child, Franchi sang for the family with his father, who played the piano and guitar.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Sun-2) At age ten, he sang a comic role as a hunchback in a school play.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Ed-1) Young Franchi formed a three-piece band at age sixteen to earn pocket money, and then later sang with a male vocal group in local jazz clubs. But, in spite of his musical talents, he soon followed his father's wishes that he pursue a career in engineering. Franchi pursued, but did not finish this training.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Nine-7) The senior Galli had been a successful businessman who owned several shops, but lost all of his assets during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and the German occupation.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Sun-2) After the war, he became friendly with a Captain in the South African medical corps who was stationed nearby. He soon followed the officer's suggestion that South Africa would be a land of more opportunity, and he immigrated to Johannesburg.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8) The family followed in 1947 (Fausta was four years old)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-9) when Franchi completed his compulsory military service at age twenty-one.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Nine-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career in South Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career in South Africa")]

When the family arrived in Johannesburg, they found that the senior Galli, a skilled wood craftsman, had established a successful furniture factory.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Sun-2) Young Franchi began using his skills as an architectural draftsman and worked for his father as a designer of commercial and industrial interiors. He also began singing in informal concerts of Italian music.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Nine-7) His voice attracted growing attention. Hearing him sing, one of the principals of the Johannesburg Operatic and Dramatic Society (JODS) tracked him down and offered him the leading role in _[The Gypsy Baron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gypsy\_Baron "The Gypsy Baron")_. (Franchi's sister Dana Valery played one of the children.) Speaking little English at the time, he learned the role phonetically. Franchi's debut was well-received, and was soon followed by leading roles in _Pink Champagne_ (_[Die Fledermaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Fledermaus "Die Fledermaus")_ in English)(1953), _[The New Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Moon "The New Moon")_ (1954), and _[The Vagabond King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vagabond\_King "The Vagabond King")_ (1955).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-JODS-10) Johannesburg's once-thriving local opera season had collapsed after WWII, and it was not possible at this time to earn a full-time wage as a singer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Bob-12)

Alessandro Rota, a successful operatic tenor in the Southern Hemisphere, came from Cape Town to Johannesburg in 1955 and helped form _The National Opera Association_. Rota began making a difference by producing operatic concerts, full acts from operas, and then full opera productions.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-14) Under Rota's tutelage, Franchi's voice matured, and he expanded his vocal range and technique.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Nine-7) About his first experience with the fledgling opera company in a production of _[Carmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen "Carmen"),_ Franchi later stated this initial experience was a disaster: He sang the tenor part in Italian, the baritone sang in Russian, and the soprano sang her role in French.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3) The company quickly matured and Rota placed Franchi in leading tenor roles in at least two successful full opera productions – Puccini's _[Madama Butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madama\_Butterfly "Madama Butterfly")_ in 1957, and then Verdi's _[La traviata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_traviata "La traviata")_ in 1959.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Bob-12) Some references also list Franchi singing lead performances in Verdi's _[Rigoletto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigoletto "Rigoletto")_ and Puccini's _[La boheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_boheme "La boheme")._[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Italy-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-16)

Sometime after the 1956 London production of _[Grab Me a Gondola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grab\_Me\_a\_Gondola "Grab Me a Gondola")_ premiered, Franchi performed in a Johannesburg stage production of the musical, and made his very first recording with the cast.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-17)

With these experiences, Franchi returned to Italy, aspiring for more opportunities to become an opera singer. While on a performing tour of South Africa, [Beniamino Gigli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beniamino_Gigli "Beniamino Gigli") had heard Franchi sing and had encouraged him and his family in this regard.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8) In 1959 Franchi made an important contact with an English agent, James Gilmore, who encouraged Franchi to meet with him if he came to London.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Lives-18)

### Return to Europe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Return to Europe")]

Franchi had some success when he was leaving Italy in 1959, such as being among the 10 finalists in a [La Scala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Scala "La Scala") competition with 250 other singers.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Durium-19) He was also offered the role of Cavaradossi in _[Tosca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tosca "Tosca"),_ which he played in a minor opera house. Looking back in 1983 about hoping to make it in Italian opera, Franchi stated that he didn't think he was in his right mind: _"I was a dreamer."_ At the time he believed he was doing well, so he sent for his wife and children. However employment opportunities ceased, and within a year Franchi was broke.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Nine-7)

Franchi then looked for work in Italy while his wife and children remained in South Africa. He began recording with [Durium Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durium_Records "Durium Records") for the popular market, having hits with _"more mio"_ and _"I tuoi occhi verde."_[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Durium-19) An album of Italian songs and several EPs and singles in Italy, London, and Canada followed (these recordings were eventually released for American audiences.) As a result of his personal appearances and recordings, Franchi began drawing enough attention to become tracked on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")._[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-20) In early 1960, Franchi played the role of Janni in the short-lived London production of _The Golden Touch._ His singing performance received favorable reviews.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Touch-21) His London agent, James Gilmore, arranged several TV appearances for Franchi, and that work (and political changes in South Africa) allowed him to return to his family in London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3)

Franchi then made several appearances on ATV's _Startime._[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-22) And then, during a two-week engagement at the London Palladium,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-23) he made two TV appearances on _[Sunday Night at the London Palladium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday\_Night\_at\_the\_London\_Palladium "Sunday Night at the London Palladium")_; a show that launched the career of many performers, and the most popular TV show in Britain.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-24) Franchi's second Palladium TV show led to a series of events that launched Franchi's American fame. Viewing his performance that night was [Norman Luboff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Luboff "Norman Luboff"), who alerted [RCA Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Victor "RCA Victor") about him. A recording audition was arranged via two taped selections sent to New York.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

With RCA approval, Luboff facilitated Franchi's signature on an exclusive seven-year [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-25) RCA Victor issued his records on the prestigious [Red Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Red_Seal "RCA Red Seal") label.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-26) He soon recorded his first RCA Victor album, in London. Plans for an American tour also soon followed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-27)

### Success in America

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Success in America")]

#### 1960s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1960s")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Sergio_Franchi_%26_Ed_Sullivan.png/250px-Sergio_Franchi_%26_Ed_Sullivan.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio_Franchi_&_Ed_Sullivan.png)

Franchi on _The Ed Sullivan Show_.

Franchi arrived in New York on September 25, 1962.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-28) RCA Victor had begun a heavy promotional campaign to launch his American career, concurrent with the release of his debut album.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-30) Franchi made his American television debut with an appearance on _[The Ed Sullivan Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ed\_Sullivan\_Show "The Ed Sullivan Show")_ on October 14, 1962;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Ed-1) and his Sol Hurok concert debut at Carnegie Hall on October 21, 1962. Singing the full length of the concert without a microphone, a New York reviewer commented on Franchi's "big, healthy voice", his penchant for ad-libbing, and his ability to establish instant rapport with his audience.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-31)

[Ed Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sullivan "Ed Sullivan") was in the audience that night and soon contracted for future Franchi appearances—including a second TV appearance on his show the following week (October 28, 1962). Franchi would later become one of Sullivan's _"two or three most favorite guests,"_, and appeared 24 times.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Ed-1) Sales for the debut record did well,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-33) peaking on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") at number 17 at the end of December.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Rovi-34) The year was concluded with successful concert appearances in Washington, D.C.'s Constitution Hall[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-35) and in Boston's [Music Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Performing_Arts_Center "Citi Performing Arts Center")[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-36)

Franchi made his nightclub debut at the Empire Room of the [Waldorf-Astoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waldorf-Astoria "Waldorf-Astoria") in New York City.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-37) While he was there he met [Metropolitan Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera "Metropolitan Opera") soprano [Anna Moffo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Moffo "Anna Moffo"), with whom he was to collaborate on two RCA Victor albums that year. Franchi continued to have many successful appearances at many large venues, including one with [Barbra Streisand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbra_Streisand "Barbra Streisand"), as well as more Sullivan television appearances.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-41)

He soon made his Las Vegas debut at the [Sahara Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara_Hotel_and_Casino "Sahara Hotel and Casino") as the opening act for [Bob Newhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Newhart "Bob Newhart").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-42) These successful performances were interspersed with multiple European events.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-43) Franchi recorded three more albums for RCA Victor (see discography), all three of which peaked on the _Billboard_ 200 pop charts in 1963.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Rovi-34) His debut album, _[Romantic Italian Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic\_Italian\_Songs "Romantic Italian Songs")_ continued on the _Billboard_ 200;[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-44) He completed the year as the opening act for [Juliet Prowse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliet_Prowse "Juliet Prowse") at the [Cocoanut Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocoanut_Grove_(Ambassador_Hotel) "Cocoanut Grove (Ambassador Hotel)").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-45)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Sergio_%26_Nick_Castle_Dancers%2C_Meredith_Willson_Show.png/250px-Sergio_%26_Nick_Castle_Dancers%2C_Meredith_Willson_Show.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio_&_Nick_Castle_Dancers,_Meredith_Willson_Show.png)

Franchi and the Nick Castle Dancers performing in the _[Meredith Willson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith\_Willson "Meredith Willson") Special_ (1964).

Franchi's February 1964 appearance at the [Sahara Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara_Hotel_and_Casino "Sahara Hotel and Casino") in Las Vegas attracted the attention of _Time_ magazine, as his performance garnered more attention and popularity than that of the star performer, including getting "standing ovations and multiple encores."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Time-46) Franchi's singing, dancing, and comedy, were then prominently featured on six television specials.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-51) Franchi made a noteworthy appearance at the "35th Annual [Chicagoland Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicagoland_Music_Festival?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chicagoland Music Festival (page does not exist)")" in August 1964,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-52) as well as starring in a performance at the Cocoanut Grove, as well as doing other events.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-53) While at Cocoanut Grove, he recorded his _Sergio Franchi - Live! at The Cocoanut Grove_ album.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-55)

1964 was a significant year for Franchi for professional and personal reasons. In a move to attract more mainstream pop audiences, RCA Victor switched Franchi from the Red Seal label to their standard black pop label. He also changed his professional representation to the [William Morris Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Morris_Agency "William Morris Agency").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-56) Although he had already received offers to star in several films, Franchi did not find a role he wished to play for a few more years.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Roles-57) Franchi then moved his family from London to a Park Avenue apartment in New York City. He also filed the first papers in declaration of his intent to become an American citizen,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Crosby-58) among other endeavors.

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Do_I_Hear_a_Waltz%3F.png/250px-Do_I_Hear_a_Waltz%3F.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Do_I_Hear_a_Waltz%3F.png)

Sergio Franchi and Elizabeth Allen in _[Do I Hear a Waltz?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_I\_Hear\_a\_Waltz%3F "Do I Hear a Waltz?")_

[Meredith Willson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith_Willson "Meredith Willson") brought Franchi to the attention of [Richard Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Rodgers "Richard Rodgers") when he was casting the leading role of the romantic Venetian shopkeeper, Renato Di Rossi, for the musical "Do I Hear a Waltz".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-60) Rodgers provided $450,000 towards the financing of the show, and Columbia Records provided $105,640. Advance ticket sales of $900,000 indicated a lengthy run, despite mixed reviews.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-61) Franchi liked the score and embraced the idea, although it meant giving up a large portion of a year's income from his concert dates.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Roles-57) The Broadway show was the focus of Franchi's endeavors until the musical closed on September 25, 1965. Reviews were generally favorable for his singing. The song "Bargaining" was especially written by Rodgers to showcase Franchi's vocal dexterity and to provide comic relief in the score.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-62) The show continued to be popular and Franchi continued success with it.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-WH-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Square-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-UN-65)

In 1965, RCA Victor allowed Franchi to appear on the [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records") cast album of _[Do I Hear a Waltz?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_I\_Hear\_a\_Waltz%3F "Do I Hear a Waltz?")_. His _Live! at the Cocoanut Grove_ album was also released early in the year. He recorded _The Songs of Richard Rodgers;_ and his evergreen Christmas album _The Heart of Christmas (Cuor' Di Natale)._ Franchi's Live! and Christmas albums both peaked on the _Billboard_ 200. Four other previously recorded albums from Europe were also released in 1965, as well two new singles. However, Franchi never had a hit single.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-66) There is some anecdotal evidence that Franchi wished to have more influence on musical choices for his singles recordings.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-67) Due to perceived injustices and dissatisfaction with RCA Victor, Franchi did not record another single for at least a year.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Over the next several years, Franchi's career continued to grow. Franchi appeared in Las Vegas and many well-known places, and opened for or was opened by many famous celebrities. He also continued to have television appearances and in general, his popularity was very high.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-75)[_[excessive citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources#Bundling\_citations "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] He also had performances internationally.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-77)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-79)[_[excessive citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources#Bundling\_citations "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_]

In 1963, Franchi turned down an offer from [Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer") to star in a film on [Mario Lanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Lanza "Mario Lanza")'s life story. Hedda Hopper quoted him as saying "If I did it well, I'd always be remembered as the man who played Lanza. If I didn't do it well, heaven help me."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-80) In 1968, he accepted a non-singing, supportive role in a [United Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Artists "United Artists") film, but soon tired of these types of positions. He stated he preferred performing on Broadway, where each night was different and a challenge to make it new.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-82)

After Franchi's Broadway role in _Waltz_, he continued to be considered for new roles on stage, but he did not return to Broadway for more than a decade. After recording several more albums for RCA Victor, Franchi's contract with the label expired in 1969 and he chose not to renew it. Instead, he signed with [United Artists Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Artists_Records "United Artists Records"), with whom he had worked with briefly before.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-83)

As the recording industry increasingly came to be dominated by the tastes of a younger generation, Franchi and many his contemporaries found their most popular reception in supper clubs.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-84)

#### 1970s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 1970s")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Sergio_Franchi_at_MGM_Grand_Hotel%2C_1974.jpg/250px-Sergio_Franchi_at_MGM_Grand_Hotel%2C_1974.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio_Franchi_at_MGM_Grand_Hotel,_1974.jpg)

Sergio Franchi with his Billboard at MGM Grand Hotel, 1974

During the 1970s, gambling was not the main attraction in Vegas. With the collapse of the musical comedy genre in movies, and the dominance of the younger generation in the recording industry—Las Vegas became a prime vacation destination for entertainment, and the place to catch live performances of stars.,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Star-85) and Franchi was no exception to this.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-88) In 1970 Franchi was voted Best Male Vocalist by _Fabulous Las Vegas Magazine._.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-90) Franchi performed successfully in many other places outside of Las Vegas as well.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-92) By 1972, Franchi had become a United States citizen.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-95)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Star-85) In general, the late 60s and most of the 70s were a period of great success and wealth for Franchi. He had many performances, concerts, appearances, records produced, and tours, both international and domestic. Some of these became an integral part of his life later on. He also engaged in activities such as advertising campaigns for private companies.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Regina-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-97)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-100)[_[excessive citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources#Bundling\_citations "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] In 1975, Franchi was the recipient of The Mario Lanza Award for outstanding achievements in the field of music.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-102)

1977 and 1978 were not particularly good years for Franchi because of medical problems, family problems, and several concert cancellations.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-103) During this period, Franchi became estranged from his wife Yvonne, and (with their children now grown) he moved back to his Manhattan apartment. Contemplating some slowdown towards a future retirement and wishing to draw his extended family closer, Franchi purchased a 240-acre estate in Stonington in September 1979.

#### 1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 1980s")]

Through the 1980s, Franchi's successes of the past two decades permitted him the opportunity to both work closer to home, and choose the length of his engagements.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3) Despite his age, reviews from this time generally regarded him as being in good physical and vocal form[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Top-104) He continued a series of successful concerts, benefits, and tours.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-106) He also received the Italian American of the Year Award in New Orleans at this time.

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c1/Sergio-Franchi-Singer.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio-Franchi-Singer.jpg)

Franchi in 1986.

Beginning on May 9, 1983, he starred in the Tony Award-winning musical _[Nine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine\_(musical) "Nine (musical)")_ and devoted 18 months to it, to generally favorable reviews. Later, in the 1980s, Franchi continued to perform at a number of popular venues in the United States.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-111) He intended to retire after his work on _Nine_, although he continued to appear in Chicago for his large fan-base there in 1985 and 1986, as well as other various places in the United States in 1987 and 1988.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-China-113) His final [Atlantic City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City "Atlantic City") appearance was in October 1987 at Trump's Castle.

In 1988, RCA re-issued the compilation album _This is Sergio Franchi_ on CD. Also in 1988, he visited the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") in Italy. The festival inspired him to produce his own 12-track 1989 album, _Encore._ which contained the 1988 Festival winner, "Perdere l'amore," and four more songs never before recorded by him.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-114)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Franchi was always attracted to the arts, and could play multiple instruments, including piano and guitar.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-115) Franchi also always carried a sketch book with him on all of his travels,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8) and in later life, devoted himself to watercolor painting in his private studio.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Ed-1)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Sergio_Franchi%27s_1955_Rolls_Royce.jpg/250px-Sergio_Franchi%27s_1955_Rolls_Royce.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio_Franchi's_1955_Rolls_Royce.jpg)

Sergio Franchi's restored 1955 Rolls-Royce

Franchi was also an avid collector and restorer of classic and antique automobiles.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-117) His collection included "25 examples of fine British, American, and Italian" cars.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Mancini-3)

On February 14, 1953, he married Yvonne Lindsey, a South African ballerina of English extraction. They had two children: a daughter, Greta Teresa; and a son, Roberto Danilo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8) They divorced on December 31, 1981, in Clark County, Nevada. Franchi married his second wife, Eva E. Simon, in New York City on June 14, 1982. Simon had emigrated with her family to America from Budapest (where she studied ballet) following the 1956 Hungarian revolt. It was a second marriage for both.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Fairytale-118)

Franchi and Simon purchased the 240-acre Farmholme property in Stonington, Connecticut in 1979.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Sun-2) He intended it to be a refuge for his retirement years. The property included several residences, and Franchi worked to make it a family compound. By 1982, Franchi had relocated his father, stepmother, and sister Mirella and her children to his estate. The dates of his mother's, father's, and stepmother's deaths are unknown. Mirella died 38 days after Franchi.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-119)

### Final illness and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Final illness and death")]

His planned return to China never occurred. His last of more than 130 television appearances was on _[Live! with Regis & Kathie Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live!\_with\_Kelly\_and\_Michael "Live! with Kelly and Michael")_ on July 4, 1989, and Franchi's last concert was at the Warwick Musical Theater on Saturday, July 29, 1989.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-120) On August 3, 1989, while rehearsing for a South Shore Music Circus concert the next day (with Pat Cooper), Franchi collapsed, was hospitalized,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-121) and the rest of his summer concerts were cancelled.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-122) Tests revealed a brain tumor and, despite radiation therapy,[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-123) Franchi succumbed to the illness. He died less than one month after his 64th birthday.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-124)

## Philanthropy and benefit concerts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Philanthropy and benefit concerts")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Sergio_Franchi_1970_Brochure_cover.bw1.jpg/250px-Sergio_Franchi_1970_Brochure_cover.bw1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio_Franchi_1970_Brochure_cover.bw1.jpg)

Franchi in a concert.

Early in his American career, Franchi's popularity drew people for major charity and benefit shows.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-125) During his dual-billing cabaret show with Barbra Streisand at the Eden Roc Hotel, they were both recruited for the American Cancer Society Benefit (MC, Bob Hope) at the Paramount Theater in Palm Beach, Florida on March 17, 1963. Along with other stars, they performed successfully before a capacity audience.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-127)

In 1965, Franchi (with [Itzhak Perlman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itzhak_Perlman "Itzhak Perlman"), [Richard Tucker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Tucker_(tenor) "Richard Tucker (tenor)") and Vivienne della Chiesa) performed at Madison Square Garden—raising $150,000 for the annual "Music Under the Stars" benefiting the American-Israeli Cultural Foundation.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Square-64) Later that year Franchi joined MC [Jack Benny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Benny "Jack Benny") and other stars for a United Nations Delegates Concert on September 10.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-UN-65)

In 1967, New York City's WNET held their annual fundraising. Franchi joined Itzhak Perlman, [Shirley Verrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_Verrett "Shirley Verrett") and [Buffy Sainte-Marie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffy_Sainte-Marie "Buffy Sainte-Marie") in the event hosted by [Tony Randall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Randall "Tony Randall").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-128) Some notable benefits at which Franchi performed during the 1970s include Milwaukee's "Fight for Sight" benefit hosted by Bob Hope at Philharmonic Hall (1971), and a star-filled Easter Seals telethon from Las Vegas at the large Sahara Hotel convention hall in 1972, where Franchi performed and made a donation[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-129) On June 3, 1984, Franchi was a featured performer at the "7th Annual Lions Sight & Hearing Telethon" on New Orleans' WGNO-TV.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-130)

One of Franchi's largest fund-raising benefit was a political event in 1982, where he helped raise over $600,000 during a three-day concert tour of Massachusetts on behalf of the re-election campaign of Governor King.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-131) In later life, Franchi donated prints of some of his watercolors for charitable sales.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-132) Franchi was a longtime supporter of the [Muscular Dystrophy Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscular_Dystrophy_Association "Muscular Dystrophy Association") and performed frequently on the annual _[Jerry Lewis MDA Telethon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry\_Lewis\_MDA\_Telethon "Jerry Lewis MDA Telethon")_. When in 1988 he was asked about his upcoming performance at Ninigret Park to benefit the Rhode Island chapter of the MDA, Franchi stated: "When you've been as fortunate as I have, you have to do something for other people." Franchi cancelled a paid performance to assist the charity, and the show was expected to net over $100,000 for the MDA.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-China-113)

Franchi was proud of both his American citizenship[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Souvenir-8) and his Italian heritage. He became active very early with the [National Italian American Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Italian_American_Foundation "National Italian American Foundation") (NIAF), and regularly performed in benefit of the Boys' Towns of Italy and the Girls' Towns of Italy.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-NIAF-133) While visiting back in Italy, he was recruited to perform what was possibly his first Boys' Towns Benefit Concert at the Fairmont Hotel in San Francisco, on May 4, 1963, of which many more followed.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-134) Franchi's support for these children's organizations also included a 1967 sold-out concert at Carnegie Hall.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-135)

As part of the 1970 celebrations of the Silver Jubilee of Boys' Towns of Italy, Franchi performed in benefits at New York's Philharmonic Hall,[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-136) and at New Orleans' Municipal Auditorium.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Italy-15) Franchi performed in New Orleans for a Boys' Towns Benefit with Dana Valery in 1974.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-137) In 1975 he held a benefit concert at the Performing Arts Center in Milwaukee for the Boys' Towns of Italy.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-138) In Pittsburgh, Franchi performed benefits in 1975 and 1977 at Heinz Hall in support of Boys' Towns.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-Boys-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-141) More boys Benefit Performances occurred in New Orleans in November 1977, occurred.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-143) along with a performance in New York on March 17, 1980.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-144) Many of the children's benefits throughout his career were in local concert halls.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-145))

### Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Awards")]

The Greater New Orleans Cultural Society honored Franchi with a special banquet (held March 12, 1982) and presented him with the 16th Annual Italian American of the Year Award.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-146) Franchi also received the [Il Leone di San Marco Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_Leone_di_San_Marco_Award?action=edit&redlink=1 "Il Leone di San Marco Award (page does not exist)") in the _Performing Arts_ (1984) from The Italian Heritage and Culture Committee of the Bronx and Westchester in New York.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-147) The Boys' Towns of Italy presented Franchi with their prestigious Michelangelo Award, and in 2001 he was posthumously awarded the title of cavaliere in the Order of Merit (Stella al merito del lavoro) by the Italian Government.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-NIAF-133)

## Presidential performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_Franchi&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Presidential performances")]

*   Franchi was invited to attend a rally for President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") to sing the [national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Star-Spangled_Banner "The Star-Spangled Banner") in 1963.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-148) Several years later Franchi revealed that he had to buy a record to learn the lyrics, and that he was completely surprised when President Kennedy asked him "Well, do you know the words?" before his performance.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-149)
*   In May 1965, Franchi went to Washington, D.C., to sing at a large [Congressional Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Club "Congressional Club") luncheon honoring [Lady Bird Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Bird_Johnson "Lady Bird Johnson").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-WH-63)
*   At President [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan")'s invitation, Franchi sang a performance at the White House Rose Garden for the State Visit of Portugal on September 15, 1983.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-150)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi#cite_note-151)

 #### [1. Teddy Pendergrass](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0671696/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Actor
    *   Composer
    *   Soundtrack

[The Nutty Professor (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117218/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

Teddy Pendergrass was born on 26 March 1950 in Kingstree, South Carolina, USA. He was an actor and composer, known for [The Nutty Professor (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117218/?ls), [Undercover Brother (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0279493/?ls) and [40 Days and 40 Nights (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0243736/?ls). He was married to [Joan Pendergrass](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4075727/?ls) and Karen Still. He died on 13 January 2010 in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania, USA.

*   
![Image 5: Freddie Mercury and Queen](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMzgyMjk2MzE1MF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwOTA3MTUxNA@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006198/?ref_=ls_i_2)  

 #### [2. Freddie Mercury](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006198/?ref_=ls_t_2) 

    *   Music Artist
    *   Actor
    *   Music Department

[Flash Gordon (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080745/?ref_=ls_knf_2)

Freddie Mercury was born on the Tanzanian island of Zanzibar. His parents, Bomi and Jer Bulsara, sent him off to a private school in India, from 1955 til 1963. In 1964, he and his family flew to England. In 1966 he started his education at the Ealing College of Art, where he graduated in 1969. He loved art, and because of that, he often went along with his friend Tim Staffell, who played in a band called Smile. Also in this band where [Brian May](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006190/?ls) and [Roger Taylor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0003547/?ls).  
  
When Staffell left the band in 1970, Mercury became their new singer. He changed the band's name into [Queen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1277102/?ls), and they took on a new bass-player in February 1971, called [John Deacon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0212577/?ls). Their first album, "Queen", came out in 1973. But their real breakthrough was "Killer Queen", on the album "Sheer Heart Attack", which was released in 1974. They became immortal with the single "Bohemian Rhapsody", on the 1975 album "A Night At The Opera".  
  
After their biggest hit in the USA in 1980 with "Another One Bites The Dust", they had a bad period. Their album "Flash Gordon" went down the drain, because the movie [Flash Gordon (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080745/?ls) flunked. Their next, the disco-oriented "Hot Space", was hated not only by rock critics but also by many hardcore fans. Only the song "Under Pressure", which they sang together with [David Bowie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000309/?ls), made a difference. In 1983, they took a year off. But, in 1984 they came back with their new album called "The Works". The singles "Radio Ga Ga" and "I Want to Break Free" did very well in the UK but a controversy over the video of the latter in the USA meant it got little exposure and flopped. Plans to tour the USA were cancelled and the band would not recover their popularity there during Mercury's lifetime.  
  
In April 1985, Mercury released his first solo album, the less rock-oriented and more dance-oriented "Mr. Bad Guy". The album is often considered now to have been a flop, but it actually wasn't. It peaked at number six in the UK and stayed on the chart for 23 weeks, making it the most successful [Queen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1277102/?ls) solo project. The band got back together again after their barnstorming performance at [Live Aid (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0261024/?ls) in July 1985. At the end of the year, they started working on their new album, "A Kind Of Magic". They also held their biggest ever world tour, the "Magic Tour". They played Wembley Stadium twice and held their very last concert in Knebworth, in front of 125.000 people.  
  
After 1986, it went silent around Queen. In 1987, he was diagnosed with AIDS but he kept working at a pace. He released a cover of the 1950s song "The Great Pretender", which went into the UK top ten. After that, he flew to Spain, where he made the magnificent album "Barcelona", together with [Montserrat Caballé](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0127481/?ls), whom he saw performing in 1983. Because Mercury loved opera, he became a huge fan of her. For him, this album was like a dream becoming reality. The single "Barcelona" went huge, and was also used as a theme song for the 1992 Olympics in Barcelona.  
  
After "Barcelona", he started working with the band again. They made "The Miracle", which was released in early 1989. It was another success, with hits such as "Breakthru", "I Want It All", "The Invisible Man" and the title track. At this point, Mercury told the band he had AIDS, meaning that a tour of the album was out of the question. After Mercury told the band, he refused to talk about it anymore. He was afraid that people would buy their records out of pity. He said he wanted to keep making music as long as possible. And he did. After "The Miracle", Mercury's health got worse. They wanted to do one more album, called "Innuendo." They worked on it in 1990 and early 1991. Every time when Mercury would feel well, he came over to the studio and sang. After "Innuendo" was released in January 1991, they made two video clips. The first one was the video clip of "I'm Going Slightly Mad", shot in March 1991. Because Mercury was very thin, and had little wounds all over his body, they used a lot of make-up. He wore a wig, and the clip was shot in black and white.  
  
Mercury's final video clip was released in June 1991. The clip, "These Are The Days Of Our Lives", later turned out to be his goodbye song, the last time he appeared on film. You could clearly see he was ill, but he still hadn't told the world about his disease. Rumours went around that he some kind of terrible disease. This rumor was confirmed by Mercury himself, one day before he passed on. His death was seen as a great loss for the world of popular music.

Grammy-winning Queen of Soul and the first woman to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Aretha Louise Franklin was born in Memphis, Tennessee, to Barbara Vernice (Siggers) and C. L. Franklin, a Baptist minister, who preached at the New Bethel Baptist Church in Detroit for over thirty years. Known as the man with the "Million-Dollar Voice", her father was one of the most respected and prominent ministers in the country, and Aretha grew up singing in church, and surrounded by local and national celebrities. She learned how to play piano by ear and soon understood the correct tones and pitches.  
  
Aretha released her first single at the age of eighteen, under Columbia Records, it reached number ten on the BillBoard charts and her first record was released in January of 1961. While working for the label, she managed to score two more R&B hits, Operation Heartbreak and Won't Be Long. However the people at Columbia often felt they didn't understand the direction Aretha wanted to go with her music, and ultimately failed to bring out her potential. In 1966, Aretha signed a contract with Atlantic Records, where she released her first legendary single, Respect, written by The King Of Soul, Otis Redding. With this single, Franklin would trigger a new vocal skill called, "call and response," which would help liven up many of her singles. While signed with Atlantic, she released three additional top ten hits, Baby I Love You, A Natural Women,and Chain Of Fools, and won her first two Grammy awards, and eight consecutive Grammys for best female R&B vocal category.  
  
Franklin had not only achieved her dream of becoming a musical sensation but stood out in the civil rights movement for her single with Otis Redding, Respect. The song helped send a message to Americans about equality, peace, and justice. Franklin continued to release pop hits throughout the decade, such as Think, I Say A Little Prayer, and Ain't No Way. After these amazing hits to many listeners she was seen as The Queen Of Soul. In the 1970s, she started recording gospel hits such as Don't Play That Song, Rocksteady, and Daydreaming. It was foreseeable that Franklin would soon stumble upon a masterpiece which became the best selling gospel album of all time, which she did in 1972 with her album Amazing Grace.  
  
In the mid '70s, even though she was releasing hit songs, she began to lose touch with her soul-pop audiences due to the disco genre making its entrance into mainstream music. In 1979, she released an album in order to gain the audience of disco lovers called, La Diva. La Diva sold less than 50,000 copies and was marked as the lowest point in Franklin's career. On June 10, 1979, her father Clarence was shot by a mugger. This left Clarence in a coma for five years and Aretha decided to move back to Detroit to take care of her father. Clarence Franklin died on July 27, 1984.  
  
In 1980, along with several other musicians such as Ray Charles and James Brown, Aretha Franklin appeared in the hit feature film The Blues Brothers. In 1982, she returned to the R&B top ten charts with her hit album Jump To It, featuring Luther Vandross. It sold more than 600,000 copies and was gold-certified, managing to stay on number one for seven weeks. In 1985, Franklin released an album which featured a unique never before heard element of rock. The album, "Who's Zoomin Who?", and soon went on to receive platinum-certified success. The album also featured a hit song with George Michael called I Know You Were Waiting For Me, and went on to sell more than one million copies. In 1987, Aretha sang the theme song to A Different World, a sitcom created by Bill Cosby, and in 1989, she released a pop album which featured Elton John, James Brown, The Four Tops, Kenny G, and Whitney Houston, called Through The Storm. In 1992, Franklin sang the song Someday We'll All Be Free for the soundtrack to the biopic film [Malcolm X (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0104797/?ls). In 1993, Aretha sang at Bill Clinton's inauguration. At a slower rate in the mid-late '90s, she continued to release albums and singles, working with new artists such as BabyFace, Jermaine Dupri, Sean "P Diddy" Combs, and Lauryn Hill along with her label, Arista Records.  
  
In 2003, she had ended the 23 year relationship with Arista and opened her own label, Aretha. Franklin released her first album on the label, A Woman Falling Out Of Love, in 2011. It marked her fifty years in show business.  
  
Aretha Franklin died of advanced pancreatic cancer on August 16, 2018, in Detroit, Michigan. She will be known as one of the most influential singers of all time, and as an activist who spoke of the world through her music, and used music as a tool for truth, justice, and soul.

A tragic fate may have given this visionary a heightened sensitivity, perception, awareness, even expansion to his obvious musical gifts that he may have never touched upon had he not suffered from his physical affliction. Whatever it was, Ray Charles revolutionized American music and was catapulted to legendary status by the time he died in Beverly Hills at age 73.  
  
Born on September 23, 1930, to Aretha and Baily Robinson, an impoverished Albany, Georgia, family that moved to Greenville, Florida while he was still an infant. It was not a cause for joy and celebration. His father soon abandoned the family and his baby brother, George Robinson, drowned in a freak washtub accident. Ray himself developed glaucoma at the age of five and within two years had lost his sight completely. A singer in a Baptist choir, he developed a love and feel for rhythms and studied music at the State School for Deaf and Blind Children, showing which brought out his talent and ear for playing various instruments, including the piano and clarinet.  
  
An orphan by his early teens, Ray joined a country band at age 16 called The Florida Playboys. He moved to Seattle in 1948 where he and Southern guitarist Gossady McGee formed the McSon Trio. With an emphasis on easy-styled jazz, Ray also played in bebop sessions on the sly. He departed from the McSon Trio and signed with Los Angeles-based Swing Time Records, becoming the pianist for rhythm and blues great [Lowell Fulson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1554090/?ls) and his band. Atlantic Records eventually picked him up. Along the road he would add composer, writer and arranger to his formidable list of talents.  
  
Ray's first R&B hit was "Confession Blues" in Los Angeles in 1949. In 1951, he had his first solo chart buster with "Baby Let Me Hold Your Hand". His amazing versatility and raw, soulful delivery quickly caught on with audiences and helped put Atlantic Records on the map. Hits like "Mess Around", "Things I Used to Do", "A Fool for You", "I've Got a Woman", "Drown in My Own Tears", and especially "What'd I Say" in 1959, pushed gospel and R&B to a wider crossover audience. He made a move into the country music arena--unheard of for a black singer--in the 1960s, doing soulful spins on [Hank Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0930729/?ls) and [Eddy Arnold](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0036425/?ls) tunes. In 1960, he left Atlantic and signed with ABC-Paramount. Under ABC-Paramount, hits poured out during this peak time with "I Can't Stop Loving You", "Hit the Road Jack", "Busted" and his beloved signature song "Georgia On My Mind".  
  
His landmark 1962 album "Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music" brought a new swinging style to country music. From there, he traveled a mainstream route--from interpreting songs from [The Beatles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1397313/?ls) ("Eleanor Rigby") to appearing in "Diet Pepsi" ads ("You Got the Right One, Baby, Uh-huh!"). He also showed up sporadically in films, playing himself in the movie [Ballad in Blue (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058935/?ls) and guest-starring in [The Blues Brothers (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080455/?ls) with [Dan Aykroyd](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000101/?ls) and [John Belushi](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000004/?ls). A television musical variety favorite with his trademark dark sunglasses and dry humor, he worked alongside such musical legends as [Ella Fitzgerald](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0280228/?ls) and [Barbra Streisand](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000659/?ls) on their very special evenings of song.  
  
It is hard to believe that with everything he accomplished, Ray also had to deal with a longstanding heroin problem. In the mid-1960s, he was arrested for possession of heroin and marijuana and revealed that he had been addicted for nearly two decades. By 1965, he had completely recovered. The man who lived life on the edge was divorced twice and had 12 children both in and outside his marriages.  
  
At the time of his death from liver disease on June 10, 2004, he was working on a recording project of duets with such performers as [Willie Nelson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005268/?ls), [Bonnie Raitt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0707248/?ls), [B.B. King](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0454475/?ls), [Elton John](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005056/?ls) and [Norah Jones](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1289528/?ls). This collaboration entitled "Genius Loves Company" led to an incisive win at the Grammy Awards--eight posthumous trophies including "Album of the Year" and "Record of the Year".  
  
A few months after his death, the critically-acclaimed feature film biography [Ray (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0350258/?ls) was released starring Oscar-winner [Jamie Foxx](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004937/?ls).

Michael Joseph Jackson was born on August 29, 1958 in Gary, Indiana, and entertained audiences nearly his entire life. His father, [Joe Jackson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1129499/?ls) (no relation to [Joe Jackson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0413690/?ls), also a musician), had been a guitarist, but was forced to give up his musical ambitions following his marriage to Michael's mother [Katherine Jackson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1808277/?ls) (née Katherine Esther Scruse). Together, they prodded their growing family's musical interests at home. By the early 1960s, the older boys Jackie, Tito and Jermaine had begun performing around the city; by 1964, Michael and Marlon had joined in.  
  
A musical prodigy, Michael's singing and dancing talents were amazingly mature, and he soon became the dominant voice and focus of the [Jackson 5](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1917778/?ls). An opening act for such soul groups as the O-Jays and [James Brown](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0113768/?ls), it was [Gladys Knight](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0460912/?ls) (not [Diana Ross](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005384/?ls)) who officially brought the group to [Berry Gordy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0330700/?ls)'s attention, and by 1969, the boys were producing back-to-back chart-busting hits as Motown artists ("I Want You Back," "ABC," "Never Can Say Goodbye," "Got to Be There," etc.). As a product of the 1970s, the boys emerged as one of the most accomplished black pop / soul vocal groups in music history, successfully evolving from a group like [The Temptations](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0291332/?ls) to a disco phenomenon.  
  
Solo success for Michael was inevitable, and by the 1980s, he had become infinitely more popular than his brotherly group. Record sales consistently orbited, culminating in the biggest-selling album of all time, "Thriller" in 1982. A TV natural, he ventured rather uneasily into films, such as playing the Scarecrow in [The Wiz (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078504/?ls), but had much better luck with elaborate music videos.  
  
In the 1990s, the downside as an 1980s pop phenomenon began to rear itself. Michael grew terribly child-like and introverted by his peerless celebrity. A rather timorous, androgynous figure to begin with, his physical appearance began to change drastically, and his behavior grew alarmingly bizarre, making him a consistent target for scandal-making, despite his numerous charitable acts. Two brief marriages -- one to [Elvis Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000062/?ls)'s daughter [Lisa Marie Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1070086/?ls) -- were forged and two children produced by his second wife during that time, but the purposes behind them appeared image-oriented.  
  
Michael Jackson died on June 25, 2009 in Los Angeles, California. His passion and artistry as a singer, dancer, writer and businessman were unparalleled, and it is these prodigious talents that will ultimately prevail over the extremely negative aspects of his troubled adult life.

Nelson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0625484/?ls), a lyricist and pianist. His father's stage name was "Prince Rogers". His parents were both from African-American families from Louisiana. They separated during his youth, which led him to move back and forth. Prince had a troubled relationship with his step-father which led him to run away from home. Prince was adopted by a family called the Andersons. Prince soon after became friends with the Anderson's son, Andre Anderson (Cymone) together along with Charles Smith they joined a band called Grand Central. Prince at the age of eighteen started working on high-quality demo tracks with Chris Moon. With these demo tracks Prince eventually ended up signing a recording contract with Warner Brothers Records and was the youngest producer associated with the label. Prince made his debut on the record label with his 1978 album, For You. It wasn't a strong successful album, however it was fair for a beginning artist and ranked 163 on the U.S. Pop Charts. Prince's next releases would tend to do much better on the charts with his singles, "Why You Wanna Treat Me So Bad?" and I Wanna Be Your Lover in 1979. This would start to introduce Prince as a person who presented sexually explicit material into the music industry. However Prince didn't begin to attract mainstream artists until he release his single, 1999. This single began to be noticed by M.T.V. viewers and this would make him a part of the main-stream music media. Prince released two more singles called Little Red Corvette and Delirious. The album featured Prince's new band, The Revolution. In 1984 Prince would release what would be seen as an admired and profound masterpiece the feature film/sound-track album, Purple Rain in 1984. Prince's father contributed to this album, by cowriting the chord sequence for a couple of his songs. Prince continued to give cowriting credit to his father on several other albums, as his famous chord sequence would be used in several of Prince's singles and albums.  
  
A lot of Prince's songs did not agree with listeners and one of his songs, Darling Nikki prompted a group of people to start a censorship organization called, Parents Music Resource Center (P.M.R.C.) as the track implemented grinding ludicrous acts such as masturbating, which stunned listeners. Prince however continued to release various other singles with the same platform his memorable releases being, Around The World In A Day, Parade, Love Sexy, and Batman.  
  
Prince released a sequel to Purple Rain in 1990 called Graffiti Bridge, a soundtrack album accompanied this movie entitled, Graffiti Bridge. The film did terrible in box-office and was nominated for several Razzie awards. Many people saw the sound-track album, as the high point of the film.  
  
In 1991, Prince assembled a new band called, The New Power Generation with this band he would release singles such as Diamond And Pearls, Cream, and Gett Off. Prince eventually changed his stage name from Prince to a symbol, which lead people to call him, "The Artist Formerly Known As Prince". Prince soon took back his old stage name.  
  
In the 1990s, Prince continued to release singles such as Came, The Gold Experience, Chaos And Disorder, and Emancipation. With the rise of the new millennium, Prince released material such as a religious album called The Rainbow Children, One Nite Alone, The Chocolate Invasion, The Slaughter House, and had a collaboration with Stevie Wonder on Stevie's single called, What The Fuss in 2005.  
  
Prince died on April 21, 2016 in Chanhassen, Minnesota, at his Paisley Park recording studio complex. He was 57.  
  
Prince will be remembered as a musician and artist who inspired millions through his music, and set an inspirational platform which others still abide by.

Marvin Pentz Gay Jr. (known professionally as Marvin Gaye; April 2, 1939 - April 1, 1984) was an American singer and songwriter. He helped to shape the sound of Motown in the 1960s, first as an in-house session player and later as a solo artist with a string of successes, earning him the nicknames "Prince of Motown" and "Prince of Soul".  
  
Gaye's Motown songs include "Ain't That Peculiar", "How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved By You)", and "I Heard It Through the Grapevine". Gaye also recorded duets with Mary Wells, Kim Weston, Tammi Terrell, and Diana Ross. During the 1970s, Gaye recorded the albums What's Going On and Let's Get It On and became one of the first artists in Motown to break away from the reins of a production company.  
  
His later recordings influenced several contemporary R&B sub-genres, such as quiet storm and Neo-Soul. He was a tax exile in Europe in the early 1980s; he released "Sexual Healing" in 1982, which won him his first two Grammy Awards on the album Midnight Love. Gaye's last televised appearances were at the 1983 NBA All-Star Game, where he sang "The Star-Spangled Banner"; Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever; and Soul Train.  
  
On April 1, 1984, the eve of his 45th birthday, Gaye was shot and mortally wounded by his father, Marvin Gay Sr., at their house in Hancock Park, Los Angeles, after an argument. Gay Sr. later pleaded no contest to voluntary manslaughter, and received a six-year suspended sentence and five years of probation. Many institutions have posthumously bestowed Gaye with awards and other honors including the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award, and inductions into the Rhythm and Blues Music Hall of Fame, the Songwriters Hall of Fame, and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

If you were to try and summarize Barry Gibb's forty-five year career in the music industry in a single phrase you would probably come up with something such as "versatile". Barry Gibb continues to remain an important, relevant figure in the music industry due to his willingness to adapt his music, his style and his image into whatever musical styling is at the fore. What makes the story of Barry Gibb so unique is that he has had a successful musical career of over forty years, continually restyling both the image and the music of the Bee Gees in order to remain relevant to the contemporary era. Barry has gone from being the front man of the soft rock/pop styling of the Bee Gees in the 1960s, to bringing the disco scene to the fore in the 70s, becoming a crooner in the 80s and reinventing his career yet again in the 1990s, as the Bee Gees enjoyed yet another reinvigoration, as their new albums and hit "One Night Only" tour proved that the music of the Bee Gees was timeless. Lasting over forty years, the Bee Gees are one of the longest running musical acts of all-time, and Barry's longevity can be attributed in part to the timelessness of his songs about unrequited love, soul-mates, people finding courage in times of dismay and above all, celebrating the short time we have on this earth.  
  
Barry's story begins on the 1st of September 1946, where he was born the second of five children to parents Barbara and Hugh Gibb. In the early 1960s Barry, and his twin brothers, Maurice and Robin, formed pop group The Bee Gees, named in tribute to two people who helped launch their career, racetrack promoter Bill Goode and a DJ named Bill Gates. It was later changed to an acronym for the Brothers Gibb.  
  
Barry and his family emigrated to Australia shortly after the birth of youngest sibling Andy, and the Gibbs performed anywhere and everywhere they could, in order to raise some pocket money. After securing a spot performing on local television shows, they were eventually signed for a record label in 1963. From the outset Barry was the primary creative force behind the music of the Bee Gees, penning the majority of their hit songs in the 1960s as well as countless other songs for other artists. In the 1970s the was a drastic change to the dynamics of the music industry, which saw singers from previous eras struggle to remain relevant. Barry helped pave the way for the Bee Gees most memorable decade, as he came up with the idea of performing in their now trademark falsetto's, as well as helping to launch the career of his youngest sibling, Andy Gibb. Barry became a mentor to the young Andy, guiding him in his initial foray into the music industry, by penning the majority of his hit singles.  
  
The 1980s saw Barry struggle to remain relevant to the music industry, as the onset of the electro-funk styling of bands such as INXS saw the Bee Gees labeled as "uncool". Barry refused to be swayed by the Bee Gees dwindling record sales, and continued to record as both part of the Bee Gees, while also making his mark as a songwriter for other artists, penning memorable hit songs for artists as diverse as Kenny Rogers, Diana Ross and Olivia Newton-John. In 1988 Barry was heartbroken when brother Andy Gibb succumbed to years of substance abuse, and died at the age of 30. Just months before in was decided that Andy would be joining the Bee Gees as the fourth member, and Andy's death took a toll on Barry for the remainder of that decade, and his musical creativity diminished.  
  
While Barry continues to record in the early 90s, it wasn't until 1997 that the Bee Gees returned to the fore, with the critically hailed "Still Waters" album. In late 1997 Barry, Robin and Maurice performed the legendary "One Night Only" concert at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States, and the DVD recording of the concert has gone on to become the highest selling music DVD in Australian history, remaining on the ARIA DVD chart for over ten years.  
  
In 2003 Maurice Gibb died of a cardiac arrest because of a congenital birth defect, bringing to a close the forty year career of The Bee Gees. However, Barry continues to remain in the public eye, as he has become more politically active, as he has generated controversy for his staunch criticism of the Schappelle Corby trial and lack of copyright protection for sound recordings in the UK. Few singers can boast having a number one record in five consecutive decades as Barry can, and with artists such as Faith No More, Wyclef Jean and Ronan Keating covering Barry's songs, Barry's timeless lyrics continue to reach out to a new generation of listeners.
